name: Form file upload → Presentations.AI summary presentation

parameters.content:
## Turn an uploaded report into a summary presentation

### How it works
Someone uploads a PDF, Word or PowerPoint file in a web form. Presentations.AI reads it and creates a presentation that keeps the sections of the report and tightens them into key slides (**Summarize** mode). It follows the report's language. When the presentation is ready, the form's last page downloads it in the browser. This usually takes 2–4 minutes, so keep the page open.

### Setup
1. Install the community node package `@presentations-ai/n8n-nodes-presentations-ai` (tested with version 0.3.2 and later). Follow [n8n's guide to installing verified community nodes](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/installation/verified-install/).
2. Create an API key at [api.presentations.ai](https://api.presentations.ai/#/apikeys) with the **Deck automation** preset, then create a **Presentations.AI API** credential with it and select it on the Presentations.AI node. Presentations.AI charges credits per slide.
3. Click **Execute workflow** and upload a test file, or activate the workflow and share the production form URL.

### Customization
Allow more file types: the node accepts PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, CSV, text, Markdown, HTML, JSON, EPUB, PNG and JPEG up to 150 MB, but not old .doc or .ppt files. Change **Preservation Mode** to Preserve to keep the report's structure, or set **Slide Count**, **Export Format** or **Brand Kit**. Turn on **Create Share Link** to give a link instead of a file. Raise **Max Wait (Seconds)** for very long reports.

### Cost and access
Anyone with the form's production URL can make presentations on your Presentations.AI credits. Share it only with people you trust, or add authentication in the Form Trigger's settings.

## 1. Upload
The form has one required file field. n8n names the binary field after the field's **Field Name**: `report`.

## 2. Create the presentation
**Input Binary Field** is `report`. **Language** is `auto`, so the deck follows the report.

## 3. Return the file
The form's ending page returns the binary field `data`, where the node puts the finished file.
